title: The Danube Dawn
subtitle: Operations Manual 101: The "Danube Dawn" is designed to serve all members of the public in the Danube basin.

trails.title: News or Rumor?
trails.description: Sometimes rigorous reports and alley whispers are one and the same.

content.text: Notice of the "Danube Dawn" Resumed Service - Vienna-Pannonian Railways

Vienna-Pannonian Railways announced yesterday that after a full year of maintenance, the "Danube Dawn" will officially resume service next Wednesday. The new train is said to drastically reduce travel time between Istanbul and Vienna, strengthening connections throughout the Danube region.

Rumors, of course, soon followed. An engineer—who wished to remain anonymous—claimed that the train's remarkable performance might not be entirely due to human work. He reported glimpsing peculiar, Critter-like entities near the engine room and wheel bearings, somewhere between a beetle and a firefly in size, dark brown in color, with two slender antennae that glowed faintly red. The workers nicknamed them "Scarlet Nightmares."

"They seem... very fond of staying close to the engines," he said. "When the machinery runs smoothly, they're lively; when it doesn't, they bunch together and start ... glowing, bright red."

Vienna-Pannonian Railways declined to comment. However, several arcanobiology enthusiasts have suggested that these beings are far from ordinary Critters. They might, in fact, be familiars of vampires—social, volatile creatures said to feed on the blood of laborers.

"This isn't a metaphor," they insisted. "It's real."

"People have long said the disappearance of the 'Danube Dawn''s former conductor was connected to a vampire. Now these Critters show up, and somehow it's the same story again ... maybe the train itself is a familiar of the vampires ..."
"Hah! If tickets weren't sold out, I'd get on board myself, maybe even catch a few to show everyone!"
"Don't joke about that ..."

...

Whether the so-called "vampire familiar theory" holds any truth or not, the "Danube Dawn" will depart on schedule. Will it truly reshape the Danube region's transport network as promised by Vienna-Pannonian Railways? Has it truly been touched by supernatural power? Only time will tell.

items.text: A train glides across snow-covered plains. The dim glow of a town beginning to emerge from the dark horizon ahead.
The "Danube Dawn"

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Stand straight.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Mmh ... ugh—ah!
A red ball tumbles from her head, unspooling a long strand of yarn that leads back to the knitting needles in the conductress's hand.
Her scarred hands do not pause their work.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Twelve seconds. Again.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Yarn is round ... How can I balance a round thing on my round head for thirty whole seconds?!

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: By standing properly. You can at least do better than that.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I've been keeping this thing on my head forever!

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Stewardess Rubuska, I trust you have more than twelve seconds of self-control in you.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: This isn't to punish you. I'm proving a point.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: A train steward's duties are to patrol the cabins, maintain decorum, and provide service.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: They do not extend to telling stories of vampires, blocking aisles with inane chatter, or hanging upside down from luggage racks.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Have I hired a stewardess or a bat?
She puts pointed weight on the word "stewardess."

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I expect you to study your handbook thoroughly, and above all else, that you keep your feet on the ground.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Pick up the yarn, wind it back. I'll begin the count again.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: ... *sigh*

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: But the passengers were all having so much fun ...
She mutters the words under her breath, but nonetheless winds up the yarn, before returning the ball to her head.
The "Danube Dawn" churns a flurry of whirling snowflakes that rush past its windows.
Passengers doze, some write letters in the dim lamplight, and others fold creases into Christmas wrapping paper.
The stewardess-in-training rubs her sore neck as she slips through the cabin, pausing to lift a dropped blanket back onto a sleeping passenger.
With a yawn, all memory of her posture training fades, as her limbs and back droop into a comfortable tilt.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Haaah ... ahhh ...

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Rubuska! The conductress let you go so soon?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: How did it go?
Aima holds an empty kettle. Her concern for the trainee's progress is genuine.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Mm ... it could've been worse ...

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Did she quiz you on the safety manual? Section Ten ...
The two stewardesses whisper as they walk side by side down the aisle, mindful not to disturb the passengers around them.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: ... Tomorrow she's going to have me balance TWO!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: It doesn't make any sense ...

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Aima, did she ever make you balance yarn?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Huh? N-no, never ...

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: But I have helped the conductress wind her yarn when she's busy.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: No matter how late work runs, she always finds time to knit.
The young stewardess drops her gaze, as if caught in a peaceful memory.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Why is she always knitting, anyway?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Don't tell me, she's planning to make the whole train a scarf?
Her companion can't help but giggle.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: She has much to handle in a day. The "Danube Dawn" wouldn't be able to run without her.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: She once told me knitting gave her a chance to "wind her thoughts."

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I'd say she's thinking about far too many things ...
She looks around at the roomful of knitted pieces, where even the tiniest ornaments on the table are dressed in finely stitched covers.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: No more hanging upside down in the cabins ... I never want to balance another ball again!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: She's always so busy. You'd think she wouldn't find time to correct all of my "little mistakes."
Rubuska reaches her desk and pulls out a stack of letter paper. One hand rummages for the lamp as she bites down on the cap of her pen and twists it off.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Is she making you copy out the safety manual again?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Mm ... no, or well, that can wait!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: I'm writing to Annabelle and the others. I'm going to drop it in the postbox at the next station. I hope it will reach them in time.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: As long as you post it before noon, it should reach Budapest in ... five days!
The young stewardess, ever quick with calculations, does the math in an instant.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Great! I promised Annabelle my letter would reach her before Christmas Eve ... Last time I told her the story of Arnold VI!
Letters were dropped into the station postboxes, and later replies came fluttering back from Budapest. Without realizing it, she had already told the stories of Arnold the Vampire I through VI.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Well, then the next story must be about Arnold VI's descendant—Rubuska I!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Rubuska I?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: What's wrong?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: N-no, nothing! Right ... next comes the story of Rubuska I.
Her pen trembles, a drip of ink swivels over the page. But the writer reacts fast enough to keep it off her clean white paper.
The story seems to be stuck like dry ink in her pen until, at last, she forces it to flow.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: ... Right then! Time to tell of the greatest vampire of this century, Arnold VI's descendant—Rubuska I.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Dear Annabelle ...

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Rubuska I was born into a mighty vampire clan, a life of plenty, joy, and laughter.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: But fate tested her early, for her strength showed itself too soon ... Hey, don't worry; every vampire must face trials in their life ...

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: My beloved, Count Arnold the Bloodthirsty, might I invite you to join us for supper? We intend to find a scrumptious human feast ...

items.speaker: Rubuska's Father
items.text: Why, it would be my honor, my lady! We vampires have crept in the shadows of this new world for too long, and I can already smell their fear.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: Oh, look who else has joined our table! Our most infamous young vampire—Rubuska!

items.speaker: Rubuska's Father
items.text: And this one too ... another shadow to linger in the night, Kolyo! A most promising vampire indeed ...

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: What a splendid age for our kind ...
The smiling mother sets plates on a table covered by a worn cloth. On them: a spoonful of beans, sauerkraut, and chunks of boiled potato.

items.speaker: Kolyo
items.text: Wow ...

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: *sigh*

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: My lady, might I request something other than these ... beans?

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: Why, my darling Buska, do you mean that you don't care for these delicious tiny human livers? They're good for a growing vampire. Besides ...
A shadow slithers up the table's edge, forming the shape of a rabbit, then a cat, a dog, a macaw ...
The shadows come alive, circling Rubuska's plate, pecking at the damp, gray-yellow beans.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: See how the shadows love them? Feast, Buska, darling; it would be impolite to refuse such a bountiful gift.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Father
items.text: Indeed! Lady Rubuska, I know you must long for the days when we lounged in the finest silks and supped on only the most tender cuts of flesh.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Father
items.text: But to be strong, a vampire must have a rich diet, including these bea—tiny livers.

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: Mm ... you are right, my lord!

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: Much better, my darling! We must sup on more than blood alone to sustain an immortal life.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Father
items.text: Savor all of life's many colors and wonders, my dear.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: Eat well, my children.
The glow of her arcane skill fades, and the small shadows sink back into the threadbare tablecloth.
Rubuska's eyes flit over her mother's hand resting on her worn gold ring, then to the plate before her—once the finest china, now chipped and cracked.
The roof leaks, the table creaks, and in the corner lies the cramped and sagging bed they share. Yet it seems to mean nothing when she returns to the cheerful smiles of her parents.
Her home is smaller now, but it is still home.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: In the still night, Arnold V prowls his lands ...

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: The beasts awake from their slumber, sniffing his outstretched hand, knowing his strength and his justice.
Tiny shadows flicker again in the worn gray corner, black silhouettes of animals hopping merrily through the dim room.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: They leap and call from dusk to the breaking of daylight, and Arnold roams with them, bringing peace to all beneath the canopy of his twilight forest ...
The children watch a Shadow Theater performance as they huddle together beneath the covers, lulled to sleep by their mother's gentle voice.
But the sweet weight of sleep is ripped from them by the hammer of gunfire.

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: Mама, it's starting again ...

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: Hush ... my child. We must stay quiet.

items.speaker: Young Rubuska
items.text: Will they leave?

Her voice is nearly a whisper tinted with fear. The gunfire erupts again, closer now, so close it seems ready to pierce the walls of their tiny sanctum.
Yet, even that whisper is enough for her mother to clamp a hand on her mouth.
The enemy has occupied their town.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: Sleep now, child. Sleep.

The hammering continues, never frequent enough to become a rhythm, never rare enough to settle. She presses her hand over her daughter's eyes. Her wavering voice whispering a promise neither believes.

items.speaker: Rubuska's Mother
items.text: It will be over soon ... Very soon.
